uncited: PRI Approximation Error Measurement quantifies the fidelity of a Pixel Ray Image (PRI) representation relative to its source unstructured grid by evaluating the sampling error at the grid's vertices.
It solves the problem of verifying that the resampling process (converting an unstructured grid to a semi-regular PRI structure) preserves the original scalar field's accuracy.
It is distinguished from general rendering error metrics by focusing specifically on the reconstruction error of the underlying data structure rather than the visual output of a ray-caster.
The method measures the approximation error of a PRI $P$ (which is a resampling of an unstructured grid $V$) by evaluating the scalar values of the original grid vertices within the PRI structure.
*   **Grid $V$:** A collection of tetrahedra.
Each tetrahedron $t$ has four vertices $v$ and a volume $|t|$.
*   **PRI $P$:** A data structure allowing trilinear interpolation of scalar values at arbitrary 3D coordinates.
Iterate over every tetrahedron $t$ in the original grid $V$.
For each tetrahedron $t$, iterate over its four vertices $v$.
Retrieve the original scalar value $S(v)$ from the grid $V$ at vertex $v$.
Reconstruct the scalar value $S_P(v)$ by performing trilinear interpolation on the PRI $P$ at the coordinates of vertex $v$.
Compute the residual error for each vertex: $|S(v) - S_P(v)|$.
8.  (Optional) Convert MSE to PSNR using standard logarithmic conversion.
*   **Error Threshold:** In the context of the simplification algorithm that generates the PRI, an error threshold determines when knots are removed.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** Vertices on the boundary of the grid must be correctly mapped to the PRI sampling plane.
A quality metric measuring the error committed when approximating a sphere, calculated as the distance from the sphere center to the vertices of each triangle.
It is used to compare isosurface extraction algorithms.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot V)$, where $N$ is the number of tetrahedra in the grid and $V$ is the number of vertices per tetrahedron (4).
The dominant cost is the trilinear interpolation for each vertex.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary space, as the error is accumulated in a running sum.
The PRI and Grid must be resident in memory.
It directly correlates with the simplification threshold used to generate the PRI.
It does not account for visual artifacts introduced during the ray-casting process (e.g., aliasing, lighting errors).
It assumes the PRI's trilinear interpolation is the ground truth for reconstruction, which may not match the actual ray-caster's sampling strategy.
*   **When to use:** When validating the quality of the PRI generation algorithm or comparing different simplification thresholds.
*   **When not to use:** When assessing the final visual quality of the rendered image; use PSNR/SSIM on pixel buffers instead.
The method originates from research on GPU-based unstructured grid volume rendering, specifically the Image-Based Modelling approach.
It was introduced to evaluate the accuracy of the Pixel Ray Image (PRI) representation, which replaces irregular unstructured grids with a semi-regular structure suitable for GPU texture storage.
